top-liquid-bond-prices-liquidity-indicat.dataset: Historical Top Liquid Bond Prices & Liquidity Indicators

columns.name: TICKER
columns.description: BondDroid® ticker symbol of the issuer. Where possible, it is kept consistent with the stock ticker of the issuer's ultimate parent.

columns.name: ULTIMATE_PARENT_NAME
columns.description: The name of the ultimate controlling company within a corporate structure of the obligor. Ultimate parent is usually not owned by any other entity and owns an obligor, directly or through other layers in the corporate structure.

columns.name: ISSUER_NAME
columns.description: The full legal name of the obligor.

columns.name: ISSUER_LEI
columns.description: The open-source 20-character, alpha-numeric code based on the ISO 17442. Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) connects to key reference information that enables clear and unique identification of legal entities. See www.gleif.com for more info.

columns.name: BONDDROID_INDUSTRY
columns.description: Issuer industry. NAICS 2017 taxonomy applied to the US and Global Issuers. This field corresponds to the NAIC 2017 5-digit industry code. See https://www.census.gov/eos/www/naics/

columns.name: BONDDROID_SECTOR
columns.description: Issuer sector. NAICS 2017 taxonomy applied to the US and Global Issuers. This field corresponds to the NAIC 2017 2-digit sector code. See https://www.census.gov/eos/www/naics/

columns.name: COUNTRY_OF_RISK
columns.description: BondDroid® issuer country of risk assigned based on a number of factors: issuer's country of domicile, the primary exchange on which its stock trades, the location from which the issuer derives the majority of its revenue, and its reporting currency. The naming convention follows ISO 3166 internatio

columns.name: REGION
columns.description: World Bank Region based on the issuer's country of risk. See www.data.worldbank.org

columns.name: BOND_DESCRIPTION
columns.description: Bond Description is a combination of a ticker, coupon and maturity.

columns.name: FIGI
columns.description: A FIGI (Financial Instrument Global Identifier) is a globally recognized, non-changing open source identifier created by Bloomberg. www.openfigi.com

columns.name: BONDDROID_INSTRUMENT_ID
columns.description: A 7-digit unique instrument identifier assigned by BondDroid.

columns.name: COUPON
columns.description: The annual interest rate that the bondholder receives from the bond’s issue date until maturity.

columns.name: COUPON_TYPE
columns.description: The type of coupon that the bondholder receives from the bond issue date until the maturity date. Possible values: Fixed Coupon, Floating Coupon, Fixed Coupon Paid at Maturity, Zero Coupon, Hybrid Coupon, Floating Rate Stepper, Fixed Rate Stepper

columns.name: MATURITY
columns.description: The date on which the principal amount of a bond is to be paid in full.

columns.name: CURRENCY
columns.description: The ISO currency in which the bond issue is denominated.

columns.name: ISSUE_DATE
columns.description: The calendar date on which the instrument was first made available to the market.

columns.name: T_BENCHMARK
columns.description: The description of the US Treasury issue most frequently used to hedge interest rate exposure the bond.

columns.name: T_BENCHMARK_CUSIP
columns.description: A 9-digit numeric or nine-character alphanumeric code that identifies a North American financial security for the purposes of facilitating clearing and settlement of trades. CGS license is required.

columns.name: T_BENCHMARK_ISIN
columns.description: A 12-character alphanumeric code that serves for uniform identification of a security through normalization of the assigned National Number, where one exists. CGS license is required.

columns.name: T_BENCHMARK_FIGI
columns.description: A FIGI (Financial Instrument Global Identifier) is a globally recognized, non-changing open source identifier created by Bloomberg. www.openfigi.com

columns.name: MARKET_SEGMENT
columns.description: BondDroid® market segment. Possible Values include: DM CorporateDM Sovereign, EM Corporate, EM Sovereign, Supranational

columns.name: AVG_DAILY_TRADE_COUNT_60
columns.description: The average number of times this bond traded in the past 60 business days.

columns.name: TIMES_TRADED_60
columns.description: The number of times this bond traded in the past 60 business days.

columns.name: TIME_SINCE_LAST_TRADE
columns.description: Number of hours since this bond traded. Possible values: 0-24, 24-48, 48-72, 72+.

columns.name: SEQ_ID
columns.description: Identifies and provides chronological ordering for each OAS signal. In combination with the instrument_ID, it uniquely identifies a set of OAS signals.

columns.name: TICK_ID
columns.description: Tick ID = Sequence ID + 'T' + tick update counter. Tick ID identifies and provides chronological ordering for each tick update for the Price, Yield and SOT and links it with the underlying OAS signal.

columns.name: RATES_TIMESTAMP
columns.description: The date and time when Price, Yield and Spread-over-Treasury are updated in line with the Benchmark Treasury and all pricing values (OAS, Price, Yield, SOT) are made available to clients. Ticks approximately every 20 seconds on the Excel API and every minute on FIX.

columns.name: SIGNAL_TIMESTAMP
columns.description: The date and time when OAS prediction was generated.

columns.name: BID_OAS
columns.description: Option Adjusted Spread level at the Bid side of the market.

columns.name: ASK_OAS
columns.description: Option Adjusted Spread level at the Ask side of the market.

columns.name: BID_PRICE
columns.description: Price at the Bid side of the market.

columns.name: ASK_PRICE
columns.description: Price at the Ask side of the market.

columns.name: BID_YIELD
columns.description: Yield at the Bid side of the market.

columns.name: ASK_YIELD
columns.description: Yield at the Ask side of the market.

columns.name: BID_SOT
columns.description: Spread-over-Treasury at the Bid side of the market.

columns.name: ASK_SOT
columns.description: Spread-over-Treasury at the Ask side of the market.

columns.name: TRIGGER_TIMESTAMP
columns.description: The date and time when BondDroid receives an input data point which triggers an OAS update.

columns.name: TRIGGER_TYPE
columns.description: The type of event that triggered an OAS update, for example, a TRACE print.

columns.name: ERROR_MEDIAN_OAS_30
columns.description: ERROR_MEDIAN_OAS_30

columns.name: DOS_OAS_BID
columns.description: The % change in Bid OAS since the previous business day's close.

columns.name: DOS_OAS_ASK
columns.description: The % change in Ask OAS since the previous business day's close.

columns.name: IS_CLOSE
columns.description: End-of-Day flag represents tick updates immediately after 3:59 PM ET & 5:59 PM ET.

columns.name: SOS_OAS_BID
columns.description: The % change in Bid OAS since the last signal.

columns.name: SOS_OAS_ASK
columns.description: The % change in Ask OAS since the last signal.

columns.name: DURATION_MID
columns.description: Modified duration of a bond that measures its sensitivity to a 1 bp parallel shift of the US Treasury rate curve. Duration_mid is calculated by fully repricing the bond to match the most recent mid signal price, assuming a $1,000 face value.

columns.name: CONVEXITY_MID
columns.description: Modified convexity of a bond that measures its curvature in the relationship between bond prices and bond yields. Convexity_mid is calculated by fully repricing the bond to match the most recent bid signal price, assuming a $1,000 face value.

columns.name: AREA
columns.description: The designation of the area being described. Canadian DAS have a "CA:" prefix to differentiate from US CBGs.

columns.name: AREA_TYPE
columns.description: The type of area specified in the area column. Canadian DAs will have 'Census Block Group' here.

columns.name: ORIGIN_AREA_TYPE
columns.description: The type of area used in the device home areas and device_daytime_areas columns. Canadian DAs have 'Census Block Group' here but both CBGs and DAs will appear in these columns.

columns.name: DATE_RANGE_START
columns.description: Start time for measurement period in ISO 8601 format of YYYY-MM- DDTHH:mm:SS±hh:mm (local time with offset from GMT).

columns.name: DATE_RANGE_END
columns.description: End time for measurement period in ISO 8601 format of YYYY-MM- DDTHH:mm:SS±hh:mm (local time with offset from GMT). The end time will be the last day of the month at 12 a.m. local time.

columns.name: DAY_COUNTS
columns.description: The frequency of each day of the week that occurred in the date range in local time.

columns.name: STOP_COUNTS
columns.description: Number of estimated stops of the adult population to this area during the date range. A stop must have a minimum duration of 1 minute to be included. The count includes stops by devices whose home area is the same as this area.

columns.name: DEVICE_COUNTS
columns.description: Number of unique devices in the adult population that stopped in this area during the date range. This includes devices whose home area is the same as this area.

columns.name: STOPS_BY_DAY
columns.description: The number of stops in this area each day (local time) over the covered time period.

columns.name: STOPS_BY_EACH_HOUR
columns.description: The number of stops in this area that began each hour (local time) over the covered time period.

columns.name: DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: The number of devices of the adult population that stopped in this area by home origin area. The area itself is included as a potential key. See Determining Home Location and Privacy is applied to this column.

columns.name: WEEKDAY_DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: This column is the same as device_home_areas except it only includes those devices that stopped in the area Monday through Friday local time.

columns.name: WEEKEND_DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: This column is the same as device_home_areas except it only includes those visitors that visited on Saturday or Sunday local time.

columns.name: BREAKFAST_DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: This column is the same as the device_home_areas except it only includes those devices that stopped in the area between 6 am and 10:59 am local time.

columns.name: LUNCH_DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: This column is the same as device_home_areas except it only includes those devices that stopped in the area between 11 am and 2:59 pm local time.

columns.name: AFTERNOON_TEA_DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: This column is the same as device_home_areas except it only includes those devices that stopped in the area between 3 pm and 4:59 pm local time.

columns.name: DINNER_DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: This column is the same as device_home_areas except it only includes those devices that stopped in the area between 5 pm and 8:59 pm local time.

columns.name: NIGHTLIFE_DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: This column is the same as device_home_areas except it only includes those devices that stopped in the area between 9 pm and midnight local time.

columns.name: WORK_HOURS_DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: This column is the same as device_home_areas except it only includes those devices that stopped in the area between 7:30 am and 5:30 pm Monday through Friday local time.

columns.name: WORK_BEHAVIOR_DEVICE_HOME_AREAS
columns.description: This column is the same as work_hours_device_home_areas but only includes devices that dwelled for at least 6 hours and excludes devices whose visit is in the same gh7 as their home location.

columns.name: DEVICE_DAYTIME_AREAS
columns.description: The number of devices of the adult population that stopped in this area by that device's primary daytime origin area. See Determining Home Location and Privacy is applied to this column.

columns.name: DISTANCE_FROM_HOME
columns.description: Median distance from home travelled by devices (of devices whose home we have identified) in meters.

columns.name: DISTANCE_FROM_PRIMARY_DAYTIME_LOCATION
columns.description: Median distance, in meters, traveled to the stopping point(s) within the area by devices from their device_daytime_area (of devices whose device_daytime_area we have identified). columns.name: MEDIAN_DWELL
columns.description: Median dwell time in minutes. Note that we are only including stops that have a dwell of at least 1 minute.

columns.name: TOP_SAME_DAY_BRAND
columns.description: Brands that the devices of the adult population that stopped in this area visited in the same day as the stop in this area. Limited to top 20. The value shown for each brand is a percentage representing: devices going to both the brand and the area / total devices stopping in the area.

columns.name: TOP_SAME_MONTH_BRAND
columns.description: Brands that the devices of the adult population that stopped in this area visited in the same month as the stop in this area. Limited to top 20. The value shown for each brand is a percentage representing: devices going to both the brand and the area / total devices stopping in the area.

columns.name: POPULARITY_BY_HOUR_TUESDAY

columns.name: POPULARITY_BY_HOUR_WEDNESDAY

columns.name: POPULARITY_BY_HOUR_THURSDAY

columns.name: POPULARITY_BY_HOUR_FRIDAY

columns.name: POPULARITY_BY_HOUR_SUNDAY

columns.description: Raw-S is the summation of sentiment of unique tweets received from credibleaccounts in a rolling 24-hour window at the time of observation

columns.description: Raw-S-Mean is the 20-day moving average of Raw-S at the time of observation.

columns.description: Raw-Volatility is the 20-day moving standard deviation of Raw-S at the time ofobservation.

columns.description: This is the statistical Z-Score of Raw-S at the observation time

columns.name: S
columns.description: Similar to Raw-S. The key difference here is that S is the exponentially timeweighted summation of tweets in the 24-hour window. Tweets arriving closer tothe observation time have a higher weight than the tweets arriving farthest fromobservation window

columns.description: The 20-day moving average of S at the time of observation.

columns.description: The 20-day moving standard deviation of S at the time of observation.

columns.description: Normalized value of S. This is CA's S-Score

columns.name: S_VOLUME

columns.name: SV_MEAN

columns.name: SV_VOLATILITY
columns.description: 20 day moving standard deviation of S-Volume at the time of observation

columns.name: SV_SCORE
columns.description: Normalized value of S-VolumeA Z-score of the S-Volume, computed like Raw-Score and S-Score

columns.name: S_DISPERSION
columns.description: Measure of the Tweet source diversity contributing to a sentiment estimate.

columns.name: S_BUZZ

columns.name: IN_MARKET_NEW_SEGMENTS
columns.description:
Predicts the likelihood that a consumer is likely to purchase a new vehicle, segment-based.
1 = Very Low 
2 = Low
3 = Medium
4 = High
5 = Very High (5x)

These segments are derived from the IN_MARKET_NEW_SCORE values, where
1= scores ranged 80-100
2= scores ranged 61-80
3= scores ranged 41

columns.name: IN_MARKET_NEW_SCORE
columns.description: Score that predicts the likelihood that a consumer is likely to purchase a new vehicle (for machine learning algorithms), Numeric values 1-100. 1 = lowest propensity, 100 = highest propensity.

columns.name: IN_MARKET_USED_SEGMENTS
columns.description:
Predicts the likelihood that a consumer is likely to purchase a used vehicle, segment-based. 
1 = Very Low 
2 = Low
3 = Medium
4 = High
5 = Very High (3x)

These segments are derived from the IN_MARKET_USED_SCORE values, where
1= scores ranged 80-100
2= scores ranged 61-80
3= scores ranged

columns.name: IN_MARKET_USED_SCORE
columns.description: Score that predicts the likelihood that a consumer is likely to purchase a used vehicle. Numeric values 1-100 (for machine learning algorithms). 1 = lowest propensity, 100 = highest propensity.

columns.description: The id of the individual product the respondent stated they purchased in the survey (for example, ProductID = 4 is Dishwasher).

columns.name: PERIOD
columns.description: The fielding period the respondent answered the survey.  For our US survey, the Period and the Year Quarter are the same.  For our Monthly US survey, Period would equal Year Month. NOTE: The primary key of a data file is: Period, RespondentID, and ProductID.

columns.name: RESPONDENTID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each respondent within a given quarter.  That is, the same RespondentID for two different quarters is not the same person.

columns.name: QTY
columns.description: Quantity*Weight.  This is the unit sample size that seen on TraQline.

columns.name: QTYP
columns.description: Quantity*Weight*Price.  This is the dollar sample size seen on TraQline.

columns.name: QUANTITY
columns.description: Number of products the respondent indicated the household bought in that particular time period/quarter.

columns.name: WEIGHT
columns.description: Demographic weight of the respondent. This is the weight we apply to balance the 150,000 quarterly respondents to the 130+ million US households.

columns.name: PRICE
columns.description: Price paid per product.

columns.description: The id of the individual product the respondent stated they purchased in the survey (for example, ProductID = 4 is Dishwasher).

columns.name: PERIOD
columns.description: The fielding period the respondent answered the survey.  For our US survey, the Period and the Year Quarter are the same.  For our Monthly US survey, Period would equal Year Month. NOTE: The primary key of a data file is: Period, RespondentID, and ProductID.

columns.name: RESPONDENTID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each respondent within a given quarter.  That is, the same RespondentID for two different quarters is not the same person.

columns.name: QTY
columns.description: Quantity*Weight.  This is the unit sample size that seen on TraQline.

columns.name: QTYP
columns.description: Quantity*Weight*Price.  This is the dollar sample size seen on TraQline.

columns.name: QUANTITY
columns.description: Number of products the respondent indicated the household bought in that particular time period/quarter.

columns.name: WEIGHT
columns.description: Demographic weight of the respondent. This is the weight we apply to balance the 150,000 quarterly respondents to the 130+ million US households.

columns.name: PRICE
columns.description: Price paid per product.

columns.name: QTY_PGT0

columns.name: PRODUCTID
columns.description: The id of the individual product the respondent stated they purchased in the survey (for example, ProductID = 4 is Dishwasher).

columns.name: PERIOD
columns.description: The fielding period the respondent answered the survey.  For our US survey, the Period and the Year Quarter are the same.  For our Monthly US survey, Period would equal Year Month. NOTE: The primary key of a data file is: Period, RespondentID, and ProductID.

columns.name: RESPONDENTID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each respondent within a given quarter.  That is, the same RespondentID for two different quarters is not the same person.

columns.name: QTY
columns.description: Quantity*Weight.  This is the unit sample size that seen on TraQline.

columns.name: QTYP
columns.description: Quantity*Weight*Price.  This is the dollar sample size seen on TraQline.

columns.name: QUANTITY
columns.description: Number of products the respondent indicated the household bought in that particular time period/quarter.

columns.name: WEIGHT
columns.description: Demographic weight of the respondent. This is the weight we apply to balance the 150,000 quarterly respondents to the 130+ million US households.

columns.name: PRICE
columns.description: Price paid per product.

columns.name: QTY_PGT0

columns.name: PRODUCTID
columns.description: The id of the individual product the respondent stated they purchased in the survey (for example, ProductID = 4 is Dishwasher).

columns.name: PERIOD
columns.description: The fielding period the respondent answered the survey.  For our US survey, the Period and the Year Quarter are the same.  For our Monthly US survey, Period would equal Year Month. NOTE: The primary key of a data file is: Period, RespondentID, and ProductID.

columns.name: RESPONDENTID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each respondent within a given quarter.  That is, the same RespondentID for two different quarters is not the same person.

columns.name: QTY
columns.description: Quantity*Weight.  This is the unit sample size that seen on TraQline.

columns.name: QTYP
columns.description: Quantity*Weight*Price.  This is the dollar sample size seen on TraQline.

columns.name: QUANTITY
columns.description: Number of products the respondent indicated the household bought in that particular time period/quarter.

columns.name: WEIGHT
columns.description: Demographic weight of the respondent. This is the weight we apply to balance the 150,000 quarterly respondents to the 130+ million US households.

columns.name: PRICE
columns.description: Price paid per product.

columns.name: RELATED_RIDESHARE_SERVICE_PCT
